_comment: Run-event dialogue: palier (miniboss) falls, roaming god encounters, a god's wrath, and flavour for shops / sacrifice altars / pact altars / the chosen character. Triggers: miniboss_<biome>, god_encounter, wrath, shop, sacrifice, altar, char_<id>.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Cyclops crashes down, its single eye gone dark. The way deeper into Hades lies open.

entries.speaker: greece_zeus
lines: One of the old earth-born brutes, felled by a soul. Hah! Keep this up, little spark.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Bhuta Lord dissolves into smoke and ash. The unseen road sinks deeper still.

entries.speaker: bali_acintya
lines: A lesser darkness, unmade. But the deeper dark of Rangda waits below. Steady yourself.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Sphinx falls silent, its riddle forever unanswered now. The night-road opens onward.

entries.speaker: egypt_osiris
lines: The guardian of the gate is overcome. But Apophis, the true terror, coils far below. Press on.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Troll topples into the frost with a sound like a falling mountain. The Helvegr leads ever down.

entries.speaker: norse_odin
lines: A jotunn's kin, broken upon the ice. Good. But the wolf still waits below, and the wolf is patient.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Tengu's wings fold and still. Deeper into Yomi's gloom the road descends.

entries.speaker: japan_amaterasu
lines: The mountain-spirit yields to you. But Orochi's eight shadows still gather below. Carry my light onward.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Jaguar Lord sinks to the bone-floor, its hunt ended. The nine levels open further down.

entries.speaker: aztec_mictlantecuhtli
lines: One of my hunters, hunted in turn. Curious. Cipactli waits at the bottom — go and meet it.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: A god of this realm stays your path — not in wrath, but with a gift held out in open hands.
Such favor is rarely given freely. Choose, and choose well.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The air turns heavy with presence. One of the dead's own gods has come to test you — and to tempt you.
Take what is offered, if you dare.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: You have lingered too long, and a god's patience is a thin and brittle thing.
It breaks now — and the dead rise at its fury. Survive them, and the spoils are yours.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Pride, was it? Or simple greed? Either way, a god has taken offense at you.
Its wrath floods this room. Endure it — and be rewarded.

entries.speaker: shade
lines: Coin still spends, even down here. Heh — especially down here. Take a look, friend.

entries.speaker: shade
lines: Everything has its price in the land of the dead, and I do mean everything. Go on, browse.

entries.speaker: shade
lines: Don't be shy. Dead men's gold still buys living men's miracles. What'll it be?

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The altar thirsts. It offers power — but only blood pays for it, and the blood it craves is yours.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Here you may trade life for strength. The dead struck such bargains often. Few ever profited.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: A shrine to one of this realm's gods stands open. Kneel, and a divine pact may be struck.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The gods of the dead are listening, here. Offer your devotion, and a boon will answer.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: You come as you are — no blade favored, no single art mastered. A wanderer, then; the most honest kind of soul to walk this road.
We shall see what you make of yourself in the dark.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: You carry yourself like one who died with a sword still in hand. The dead respect a warrior — right up until they drag one down.
Let us see whether your steel outlasts your pride.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: A hunter's eyes — always measuring the distance. You will need them; nothing in these realms wishes to be caught.
Aim true, and even the dark may learn to fear you.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Light on your feet, and quick to flee — there is no shame in that. The swift are the ones who live to walk the road again.
Run well, then. The dead are patient, but they are slow.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Something far beneath the floor of the world stirs — and, strangely, it approves of you. A whisper with no mouth brushes your mind: *little crack... little flaw... climb, and let the light in.*
A power you did not earn wells up into your hands. Take it, wanderer. Try not to wonder why it was offered.
